claim: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia opens 09:30-18:00 daily (last entry 17:30), adult RM20, closed only on the two Hari Raya.
quote: Galleries 9.30 am - 6.00 pm daily, last admission 5.30 pm. Adult RM20. Closed on Hari Raya Aidilfitri and Hari Raya Aidiladha.

claim: National Museum (Muzium Negara) open 09:00-17:00 daily, adult RM2, child/senior RM1, walk-in tickets only.
quote: The National Museum is open every day, 9.00 am to 5.00 pm. Cutoff for admission 4.30 pm. Adults RM2, children and seniors RM1. Does not sell tickets online.

claim: National Textile Museum open 09:00-17:00 daily, RM5 standard / RM2 Malaysian adult, free under 12; displays batik, songket and ethnic dress.
quote: National Textile Museum: 9am-5pm daily. RM2/adult Malaysians, RM5/adult standard, free for children under 12. Houses local textiles, ethnic adornments and traditional costumes.

claim: KL City Gallery open 09:00-18:30 daily, RM10 admission with RM5 redeemable, featuring a giant city-model light-and-sound show in Dataran Merdeka.
quote: 9:00am - 6:30pm daily. RM10, RM5 redeemable at ARCH Gift Shop and Cafe. The Spectacular City Model Show measures 40ft x 50ft.

claim: Bank Negara Malaysia Museum & Art Gallery is free, open 10:00-17:00 Tue-Sun, with six galleries including a major Southeast Asian numismatics collection.
quote: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10am-5pm, closed Mondays. Admission free. Six galleries including the Numismatics Gallery, one of Southeast Asia's most extensive currency collections.

claim: Ilham Gallery is free, open 11:00-19:00 Tue-Sat and 11:00-17:00 Sun (closed Mon), showing contemporary Malaysian and Southeast Asian art in Ilham Tower, KLCC.
quote: Tuesday to Saturday 11am-7pm, Sunday 11am-5pm, closed Mondays and public holidays. Admission free. No. 8 Jalan Binjai, Ilham Tower.

claim: Petrosains Discovery Centre is a science centre on Level 4 of Suria KLCC in the Petronas Twin Towers, open Tue-Sun (closed Mon except holidays).
quote: Petrosains, Level 4 Suria KLCC. Open Tuesday to Sunday; closed Mondays except school holidays and public holidays.

claim: Tourism Malaysia's official guide indexes KL's notable museums and galleries beyond the headline ones.
quote: Must-visit museums and galleries in KL.

claim: Thaipusam at Batu Caves draws around 1-2 million people; devotees carry kavadi, undergo body-piercing and climb the 272 steps, with a silver-chariot procession from Sri Mahamariamman beforehand.
quote: Thaipusam 2026 falls on 1 February. Devotees carry kavadi, pierce skin, tongues and cheeks, and climb 272 steps. The Silver Chariot procession departs Sri Maha Mariamman Temple.

claim: For Thaipusam 2026 free KTM Komuter rides and free Rapid KL shuttle buses run on 31 Jan-1 Feb to handle the crowds at Batu Caves.
quote: Free KTM Komuter rides and increased train services on 31 January and 1 February 2026. Rapid KL provides free shuttle bus service to Batu Caves.

claim: Malaysia 2026 holiday dates: Chinese New Year 17-18 Feb, Thaipusam 2 Feb, Hari Raya Aidilfitri 21-22 Mar, Hari Raya Haji 27 May, Wesak 31 May, Merdeka 31 Aug, Deepavali 8 Nov.
quote: Chinese New Year 17-18 February. Thaipusam 2 February. Hari Raya Aidilfitri 21-22 March. Hari Raya Haji 27 May. Wesak Day 31 May. Merdeka Day 31 August. Deepavali 8 November 2026.

claim: Malaysia's 2026 cultural festival calendar covers Thaipusam, CNY, Hari Raya, Wesak, Merdeka and Deepavali across the multicultural communities.
quote: Malaysia Festivals Guide 2026 - cultural events and celebrations including Thaipusam, Chinese New Year, Hari Raya, Deepavali.

claim: Deepavali falls on Sunday 8 November 2026 in Malaysia (observed nationwide except Sarawak, with a 9 Nov holiday in most states).
quote: In 2026, Deepavali falls on Sunday 8 November. Observed as a national holiday except in Sarawak.

claim: During Deepavali, Brickfields' Little India and Sri Kandaswamy Temple light up with garlands, lights and processions; open houses are central to the celebration.
quote: During Deepavali, Sri Kandaswamy Temple turns Brickfields into a festival of light, colour and joy, decked out in twinkling lights and garlands.

claim: Wesak Day 2026 is 31 May; major KL celebrations centre on the Maha Vihara temple in Brickfields with a float parade.
quote: Wesak Day 2026. Largest celebrations at Maha Vihara Temple in Brickfields, ending with a parade of decorated floats.

claim: Merdeka (National) Day is 31 August 2026 (a Monday), with the national parade at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur.
quote: Merdeka Day 31 August 2026. The national parade and ceremony are held at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur.

claim: KL Festival is the city's official downtown arts festival.
quote: KL Festival - bringing people to the heart of Kuala Lumpur.

claim: KL Festival 2026 runs 6-31 May across 25 venues with 80+ events and ~90% free programming, tied to Visit Malaysia 2026.
quote: KL Festival running 6 to 31 May 2026, a 26-day festival across 25 venues with more than 80 events. About 90% of the festival is free.

claim: DiverseCity is KL's International Arts Festival, a month-long programme of theatre, dance, music and visual arts.
quote: DiverseCity: Kuala Lumpur International Arts Festival celebrates the arts in all its forms through a month-long festival.

claim: 2026 is Visit Malaysia Year, with an unusually loaded calendar of festivals and signature events in Kuala Lumpur.
quote: Festival Kuala Lumpur 2026 - signature events tied to Visit Malaysia 2026.

claim: Central Market (Pasar Seni), an 1888 wet market turned crafts hall, opens 10:00-21:30 daily with free entry and sells batik, songket and handicrafts.
quote: Central Market open daily 10:00 AM to 9:30 PM, entry free. Showcases batik, songket, wood carvings, calligraphy and jewellery. Built 1888.

claim: Petaling Street is Chinatown's lantern-lined market street, with goods by day and hawker food at night, roughly 10:00 till late.
quote: Petaling Street, the heart of Chinatown, lined with red lanterns; market goods and food stalls, busy from late morning until late at night.

claim: Sri Mahamariamman, built 1873, is KL's oldest Hindu temple, free entry, open roughly 06:00-20:30, in Chinatown.
quote: Sri Mahamariamman Temple, built in 1873, is the oldest Hindu temple in Kuala Lumpur. Open daily from 6am to 8:30pm. Entrance free.

claim: Guan Di Temple, a Taoist temple built 1888 in Chinatown, is free to enter and open roughly 07:00-19:00.
quote: Guan Di Temple, built in 1888, is a historic Taoist temple in Chinatown. Open daily 7am to 7pm. No entrance fee.

claim: Kampung Baru is the last Malay village in central KL; its Saturday-night-into-Sunday market offers Malay street food beneath the Twin Towers skyline.
quote: Kampung Baru, the last Malay enclave in KL city centre, with its village-style Sunday market of Malay specialties against the Petronas Twin Towers backdrop.

claim: Ramadan bazaars run during the fasting month (≈late Feb-Mar 2026); Kampung Baru's is iconic for lemang, rendang and bubur lambuk.
quote: During Ramadan, Kampung Baru transforms into a bustling marketplace with lemang, rendang, roti jala and bubur lambuk, set against the Petronas Twin Towers.

claim: Royal Selangor Visitor Centre offers free entry with live pewtersmithing, a museum and shop, plus paid hands-on workshops.
quote: Royal Selangor Visitor Centre - live pewtersmithing demonstrations, museum, retail showroom and workshops.

claim: Royal Selangor's School of Hard Knocks workshop (craft a pewter dish, keep it plus apron and certificate) costs RM75; the larger Foundry workshop RM180.
quote: School of Hard Knocks lets you craft a simple pewter dish, take home your masterpiece, apron and certificate. RM75 per person; Foundry RM180.

claim: myBatik runs ~45-minute hands-on batik painting workshops with materials included, family-friendly, located behind the National Zoo in Ampang.
quote: myBatik - 45-minute hands-on workshop to learn to paint a traditional Malaysian batik and bring home your creation, located behind National Zoo.

claim: Jadi Batek, a large central-KL batik gallery, runs walk-in batik classes from RM22 (mini) up to RM250-550 for scarves/pareos, with tote bags ~RM68.
quote: Mini Batik RM22 (20 min), Small RM38-48, Standard RM78-98, Tote Bags RM68-78, Scarves/Pareos RM250-550.

claim: Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur on Jalan Conlay offers live batik and songket demonstrations, a craft museum, Karyaneka boutique and a batik-making craft village.
quote: Kuala Lumpur Craft Complex - batik, songket, woodcarving, the Karyaneka Craft Boutique, a Craft Museum and Craft Village for batik-making.

claim: Saloma Theatre Restaurant pairs a buffet with an 18-dancer cultural show spanning Malay, Chinese, Indian and Portuguese dances.
quote: The 18-member Saloma Dancers present Minangkabau, Chinese, Indian and Portuguese dances in traditional costumes.

claim: The Malaysia Tourism Centre (MaTiC) stages a short traditional cultural dance show as a low-cost alternative to a dinner show.
quote: Cultural Show at MaTiC - live traditional cultural dance performances.

claim: Istana Budaya is Malaysia's national theatre, home to the resident dance company, National Symphony Orchestra and traditional makyong, with a public events listing.
quote: Istana Budaya - home of the Residence Artists (Dance), the National Symphony Orchestra and the Orchestra Traditional Malaysia, including makyong theatre.

claim: KLPac (Kuala Lumpur Performing Arts Centre) in Sentul is an independent arts centre in a heritage building staging theatre, dance and music.
quote: klpac is Malaysia's only fully-integrated arts centre in a 124-year-old heritage building, with theatre, music, dance and contemporary art forms.

claim: MUD: Our Story of Kuala Lumpur is a one-hour musical on KL's 1880s tin-mining origins staged at the heritage Panggung Bandaraya; the original run priced tickets ~RM53-85 and closed in 2017.
quote: MUD at Panggung Bandaraya, the longest-running theatre show in the country, staged its final show on 30 April 2017. Regular RM84.80, with MyKad RM53.

claim: MUD ran twice daily for years as a Visit KL project produced by Enfiniti, an unusual continuous-run model for a musical.
quote: KL has a play that's been running twice every day for the past 2 years - MUD, a Visit KL project.

claim: MUD KL has been restaged by Enfiniti and billed as KL's longest-running musical, with tickets typically in the RM60-85 range.
quote: Meet the faces behind KL's longest running musical: MUD KL, produced by Enfiniti.

claim: GMBB is a creative community mall in Bukit Bintang that hosts independent arts and cultural programming.
quote: GMBB - art in Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur; a creative community mall.

claim: KL's driest, sunniest window is June-August (~125 mm/month, under 10 rain days); November is the wettest at ~370 mm.
quote: Best time to visit is the dry season June to August, rainfall ~125-127mm with under 10 rainy days. Avoid November, the wettest month at 373mm.

claim: In June 2026 the EUR-MYR rate was about 1 EUR = RM4.70.
quote: Mid-market EUR to MYR rate around 4.69-4.70 in June 2026.

claim: Petrosains admission ranges roughly RM7-28 depending on age and residency, with foreign visitors paying more than Malaysians.
quote: Petrosains ticket prices range from RM7 to RM28 depending on age and resident status; non-Malaysians pay 10-15 MYR more.
